PureBloom Cosmetics plc makes vegan, cruelty-free skincare products sold through UK supermarkets, its own website and 30 PureBloom stores. Its mission is 'beauty that does no harm'. Its products are priced about 20% above mass-market brands.

subject: A-Level Business
topic: 3.2.1 Understanding management, leadership and decision making
scenario:
Background
Jordan Reid founded Apex Arena Ltd in 2019 at the age of 23. Apex runs esports tournaments - competitive video-gaming events - in a converted warehouse in Manchester that holds 2 000 spectators. Every event is also streamed online. Apex earns revenue from tickets, sponsorship and advertising on its streams.

Apex has grown quickly. Revenue rose from £0.4m in 2020 to £3.6m in 2024. Jordan makes almost every important decision himself, often very quickly. He says: 'In this industry, if you wait for a report, someone else has already done it.' Apex was the first UK organiser to use virtual-reality viewing for online audiences.

People
Apex has 24 full-time staff and about 150 event staff on zero-hours contracts, who work as stewards, technicians and caterers at events. Event staff turnover is high (see Appendix B). Several full-time managers have left, complaining that Jordan does not let them make decisions.

The Northern Showdown
Apex is planning its biggest event yet, the 'Northern Showdown'. Jordan must decide whether to hold it in person in a hired 10 000-seat arena or as an online-only event. The forecasts are shown in Appendix A.

A new arena
Jordan wants to build Apex's own 5 000-seat arena at a cost of £3m. He is considering two ways of financing it.

Option 1: venture capital. A venture capital firm would invest £3m in return for 35% of Apex's shares and two seats on the board.

Option 2: a £3m bank loan at 8% interest a year, repayable over 10 years and secured on Apex's assets.
question: Analyse how Jordan's leadership style may have contributed to Apex Arena Ltd's rapid growth.

a clear vision from the founder gives direction to a small team

level_descriptors.descriptor: An excellent response overall that is fully focused on the key demands of the question. Demonstrates a depth and range of knowledge and understanding that is precise and well selected in relation to issues in the question; demonstrates analysis throughout which is well developed, is applied effectively to the context and considers a balanced range of the issues in the question; makes judgements or provides solutions which are built effectively on analysis, show balance and have a clear focus on the question as a whole throughout.

A good response overall that focuses on many of the demands of the question. Demonstrates a depth and range of knowledge and understanding of issues in the question; demonstrates analysis which is well developed, applied effectively to the context and considers a range of issues in the question; makes judgements or provides solutions which are built on analysis, show balance and address the question as a whole.

A reasonable response overall that focuses on some of the demands of the question. Demonstrates a limited knowledge and understanding of a range of issues in the question or a good knowledge and understanding of relatively few issues in the question; demonstrates analysis which is developed, applied to the context and considers some of the issues in the question; makes judgements or provides solutions which are built on analysis, but lack balance and are not fully focused on the question as a whole.

A limited response overall with little focus on the demands of the question. Demonstrates a limited range and depth of knowledge and understanding of issues in the question; demonstrates analysis with little development, mainly descriptive application to the context and considers a limited number of issues in the question; makes judgements or proposes solutions which have limited links to analysis or limited focus on the question as a whole.

examiner_principles: Higher levels need balance: arguments on both sides AND a judgement that weighs them up - not a summary or restatement (2024/2025 P3 reports).
The judgement must answer the precise question set and flow from the arguments made; new points introduced in the conclusion are not rewarded.
A strong judgement explains what the answer depends on, linked to the context, and which argument is more significant and why.
Flawed analysis cannot support credit-worthy evaluation - a conclusion based on a false premise is not justified.
'All businesses' / 'any business' questions need context through contrasting scenarios or real examples (e.g. fast-moving tech vs slow-moving furniture).
Quantity is less important than focus: two well-developed, balanced arguments with a weighed judgement can reach the top level.
